summary: Backend testing for Ember & Oak Smart Restaurant API. Executed 23 pytest tests covering health, seed data (menu/tables), auth (signup/login/me/owner-auto-promote), RBAC (admin/customer/staff/kitchen), Menu CRUD, Order flow with bill math (tax 5% + service 5%), inventory auto-decrement, order status transitions with customer notifications, reservations, queue, all 5 AI endpoints (recommendations, weekly-insight, forecast, inventory-alerts, chat SSE stream), and analytics summary. All 23 tests passed. Two minor test-script bugs were self-fixed (EmailStr rejects .test TLD; backend lowercases emails).

minor.issue: Emails are silently lowercased server-side. Not a bug, but callers using exact-match comparison must lowercase. Documented in tests.
Uses substring match (inv.name.lower() in item.name.lower()) which is fragile: an inventory row named 'Corn' would decrement for ANY item containing 'corn'. Consider explicit item->inventory mapping.
date/time are free-form strings; no validation of format or future date.
Errors in the stream are emitted as `data: [ERROR] ...` rather than an HTTP error, so clients cannot distinguish success/failure by status code. Acceptable for streaming but worth noting.

action_items: Consider adding an explicit menu_item -> inventory_item mapping instead of substring name match in the inventory decrement logic in create_order().
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~690 lines and mixes auth, menu, orders, inventory, staff, reservations, queue, notifications, analytics and AI wiring - consider splitting into routers (routes/auth.py, routes/orders.py, ...) once >700 lines.
Inventory decrement uses fragile substring matching on item names (line ~341).
OAuth session cookie is set with samesite='none'; secure=True which is correct for cross-site preview URLs but will fail on plain-http local dev.
push_notification uses mutable default None then `or {}` - fine, but consider `meta: Optional[dict] = None` type hint (already correct usage).
No pagination on /orders, /reservations, /notifications - limit(500/50) hardcoded. Acceptable for MVP.
PATCH /api/orders/{id}/status accepts a raw dict; add a Pydantic model with a Literal[...] to auto-validate.
